evidence.title: About Us | Stripe
evidence.highlight:
About Us | Stripe

Stripe is a technology company focused on improving the conditions for economic growth and prosperity.

We build programmable financial infrastructure, rethinking from first principles how financial services should work, to make it easier and cheaper for any business to start and scale.

More than 5 million businesses build on Stripe, spanning the economic frontier—from solo founders to established enterprises—united by a practical focus on growth. The most ambitious companies in the world use Stripe as core infrastructure to grow faster. They process trillions of dollars a year on Stripe, equivalent to around 1.7% of global GDP.

While economic growth makes everyone better off, open markets also enable greater variety. When any business can easily serve a global customer base, the quality and diversity of products in the world increase, and craft and creativity are unleashed into the smallest niches.

Our own growth is wholly contingent on the success of the businesses building on Stripe. We therefore invest back into our technology at an unusual rate. We make upgrades to our products every single day to deliver compounding gains to our customers. We maintain some of the most reliable APIs on the internet. We build entirely new pieces of financial infrastructure to enable new ideas. And our significant advances in risk and fraud infrastructure over many years are making the internet economy safer and more accessible.

#### Learn more about Stripe’s products.

What is Stripe?

Stripe is programmable financial infrastructure that helps you build and run a global business. You can use Stripe to accept payments, manage revenue, prevent fraud, move money across borders, and access a suite of developer tools and APIs. Stripe processes trillions of dollars annually for companies ranging from early-stage startups to large enterprises.

What does Stripe do?

Stripe helps businesses of all kinds accept payments globally, prevent fraud, automate revenue management, move and manage money, monetize payments and financial services, and operate across borders.

What types of businesses use Stripe?

Businesses of every size and model use Stripe—from early-stage startups to global enterprises, across retail, travel, AI, insurance, SaaS, nonprofits, online marketplaces, and more.

How does Stripe support AI businesses and agentic commerce?

Stripe is the economic infrastructure for AI. Whether you’re monetizing an AI product, making your catalog discoverable to AI agents, or building agents that can transact on your behalf, Stripe can support it—from flexible billing models to agentic checkout and developer tools built specifically for how agents work.

# Stripe builds out the economic infrastructure for AI with 288 launches 

 April 29, 2026 

- New partnership with Google will allow businesses to sell inside AI Mode and the Gemini app 
- Stripe launches wallets for agents, powered by Link, and support for new AI-native business models 
- Major expansion to Stripe Treasury, including instant, free money transfers between businesses on Stripe 

SAN FRANCISCO—Stripe today announced 288 new products and features at Stripe Sessions, its annual customer conference, as the company builds the economic infrastructure for AI. That means accelerating AI companies’ growth, helping enterprises adapt to AI, preventing fraudsters from stealing tokens, and empowering agents as economic actors.

...

The Agentic Commerce Suite now supports Google

Last year, Stripe launched the Agentic Commerce Suite, a single integration that lets businesses sell their products inside AI apps. Kate Spade, Best Buy, and Coach are among the businesses already building with the Agentic Commerce Suite.

Today, Stripe announced a partnership with Google that will allow businesses to sell to consumers inside AI Mode and the Gemini app. Businesses like Quince, Fanatics, and JD Sports are coming soon. This follows similar partnership announcements with OpenAI, Microsoft, and Meta. 

Stripe is also bringing the Agentic Commerce Suite to platforms, so businesses on Wix, BigCommerce, WooCommerce, and more can easily sell to customers inside AI apps.

...

To solve this, today

...

Massive expansion of Stripe Treasury, with instant, free money transfers between US businesses on Stripe

There’s a new breed of business building on Stripe: lean hyperscalers, growing revenue faster than ever and with a global customer base from the start. Their feedback has been consistent: they don’t just want Stripe to handle the money coming into their business, but to serve as their entire financial stack.

Today, Stripe introduced the new Stripe Treasury: a global business account that allows companies to hold funds in 15 currencies and move money around the clock.

Businesses building on Stripe make payments to each other 4.8 million times a day. With Stripe Treasury, those transactions are now free and instant for US businesses.

In addition, businesses can now:

- Operate Treasury through AI services like ChatGPT 
- Earn rewards on fiat and stablecoin balances 
- Get 2% cashback on card payments 
- Pay out to recipients in 100 countries with fiat, 160 with stablecoins

...

Stripe Projects is now available to everyone, and includes new partners

Stripe Projects lets developers or their agents sign-up for, purchase, and integrate all the services they need to deploy products to the internet, directly from wherever they write (or prompt) code. It’s one of Stripe’s most highly anticipated products, with thousands of developers joining the waitlist in the first two days after the preview announcement last month. 

As of today, Stripe Projects is available to all. 

Stripe also announced 14 new partners for Stripe Projects, including Render, Twilio, Sentry, WorkOS, Browserbase, GitLab, and ElevenLabs. These partners join existing Projects partners for a total of 32 providers including Vercel, Clerk, Supabase, Hugging Face, and Cloudflare.

...

Beyond the headline announcements, Stripe announced 288 products and features today at Stripe Sessions. To see the full list, visit the Stripe blog.

evidence.title: FedEx Dataworks and Stripe to join forces to reduce friction in global commerce for SMBs
evidence.highlight:
FedEx Dataworks and Stripe to join forces to reduce friction in global commerce for SMBs

# FedEx Dataworks and Stripe to join forces to reduce friction in global commerce for SMBs 

 October 6, 2026 

The long-term collaboration will create new solutions powered by supply chain intelligence and financial infrastructure.

MEMPHIS AND SAN FRANCISCO—Today, FedEx Dataworks and Stripe announced a long-term, strategic collaboration to help reduce friction in global commerce by combining signals from the global FedEx network and Stripe financial infrastructure. The first joint solution is planned for launch in early 2027. The two companies plan to leverage their respective platforms to expand access to financing for tens of thousands of small- and medium-sized businesses (SMBs). Additionally, FedEx will begin using Stripe as an option to process payments, adding more than 50 new payment methods to their checkouts through Stripe.

...

Securing capital remains a persistent hurdle for logistics-heavy SMBs. Traditional financing models rely on bank statements and credit scores, often overlooking operational indicators such as shipment activity, inventory movement, and fulfillment performance. By leveraging supply chain intelligence from FedEx Dataworks to help inform financing analysis with Stripe Capital, Dataworks and Stripe are seeking to close that gap and enable FedEx SMB customers to access funding that better reflects how they operate. With these real-time operational signals, Stripe will be better positioned to evaluate, approve, and deploy tailored funding more quickly than traditional lending processes, eliminating the friction for SMBs.

...

FedEx will also use Stripe to expand payment options for FedEx customers globally, adding more than 50 new payment methods to FedEx checkouts. With a wider variety of local payment methods, FedEx can help remove checkout friction so customers can pay how they prefer.

This announcement marks the beginning of a strategic, long-term collaboration between FedEx Dataworks and Stripe, laying the foundation for the next generation of business solutions powered by FedEx Dataworks logistics signals and Stripe’s financial infrastructure. As the collaboration evolves, both companies expect to scale these capabilities to meet the needs of increasingly complex global enterprise.

evidence.title: New ways for fintechs to move money and expand globally
evidence.highlight:
# New ways for fintechs to move money and expand globally 

 October 16, 2026 

 

 Neetika Bansal Business Lead, Money as a Service 

Many of the world’s leading fintechs use Stripe to build and scale, including 32 of the Forbes Fintech 50 (and counting). As these businesses expand into new markets, they need to deliver the same fast, reliable experience everywhere while supporting local payment methods, navigating local compliance requirements, and integrating new banking partners. 

We’re introducing three updates to help fintechs launch products and grow internationally more easily: simpler payout management with Stripe Global Payouts, support for stablecoin cards in more countries, and unified APIs for building global financial products. 

Here’s what’s new.

...

## Send payouts to recipients in more than 160 markets

We’ve expanded Global Payouts to more markets and made it easier to set up and manage. Businesses can now send instant stablecoin payouts to recipients in 160 markets and traditional currency payouts to recipients in more than 100, directly from the Stripe Dashboard.

Fintechs can also use Global Payouts programmatically—by embedding hosted forms or integrating with flexible APIs—to enable use cases like loan disbursements, remittances, investment withdrawals, and neobank cash-outs within their products. Turo, for example, uses Global Payouts to send claims payments. The company has processed over $160 million, with a 99.5% payout success rate.

...

## Issue stablecoin cards in more countries

Stripe is launching stablecoin card issuing in 27 EU countries, bringing availability to more than 65 countries worldwide. We plan to expand to 100 countries by the end of 2026. With stablecoin cards on Stripe Issuing, fintechs can offer cards that draw from stablecoin balances held in a custodial wallet, noncustodial wallet, or Stripe financial account. When cardholders make a purchase, Stripe automatically converts their stablecoins into the local currency at the point of sale; merchants can accept these payments just like a traditional card payment.

Fintechs can use Issuing to launch a global stablecoin card program that works across markets with one integration, rather than connecting separate providers for card issuing, currency conversion, KYC and KYB verification, fraud management, and customer support. 

Stripe Issuing already powers more than 400 million cards worldwide across commercial and consumer card programs. Stablecoin cards extend that infrastructure to fintechs and platforms building with stablecoins, enabling them to scale globally and reach a larger customer base.

...

## Grow your business on Stripe

Over 1,500 fintechs on Stripe serve customers in more than 200 countries and territories. With Stripe’s unified stack, they don’t need to integrate and manage multiple vendors. Instead, they can use a single integration to build global financial products that support money movement, storage, and payment use cases while they continue to expand across markets.

evidence.title: Stripe Careers | Shape the Future of the Global Economy
evidence.highlight:
Stripe Careers | Shape the Future of the Global Economy

# Implement the conditions for prosperity

## Our mission is to increase economic growth. At Stripe, you can make that happen.

We exist to increase economic growth, and we pursue it on every front: by building tools that make it easier and cheaper for ambitious businesses to start and scale, by publishing ideas that advance progress, and by creating the economic infrastructure for AI. Your work will define how the world transacts.

...

What does it take to do well at Stripe?

The bar at Stripe is high, and the people who do well here tend to share a few traits. We find that success depends less on background and more on how Stripes approach their work and handle the challenges that inevitably arise at a fast-moving and dynamic company. Successful Stripes tend to be motivated by our mission. That’s what fuels their ambition and their sense of ownership, which extends beyond their own expertise. At Stripe, we’re in this together, and you’ll fix things that don’t “belong” to you. People who thrive here also tend to choose challenge over comfort. When something doesn’t add up, they get curious about why, and they change their mind when the evidence shows they were wrong.

What does career growth look like at Stripe?

Fast, if you seek it out. Stripe gives people ownership early, which means you could find yourself leading significant work sooner than you would elsewhere. Promotions are tied to demonstrated impact, not tenure. We invest in development through stretch projects, direct feedback, and options for internal mobility.

What should I expect during the Stripe hiring process?

Most processes include a recruiter screen, a technical or skills-based assessment, and a series of interviews with the team you’d be joining. Timelines vary by role, level, and location—some move in a few weeks, others take longer. We try to work quickly and give clear feedback at every stage.

How do I know if a Stripe recruiter contacting me is legitimate?

Stripe recruiters reach out through official channels—LinkedIn or an @stripe.com email address—and will never ask for payment, personal financial information, or login credentials at any point in the process. If something feels off, trust that instinct.
